Find out what's going on in the world with a news bulletin designed for children, featuring stories that are relevant and easy to understand.
Meemaw meets Dale's ex-wife while Sheldon is forced to work on a group project with reluctant college students.
A naughty red panda mom makes a play for attention, a moose with a nasty cough, and a cherished cheetah beats the odds and hits a milestone!
Budding lawyer Rafe is saving for a new iPad, but his younger brother isn't convinced he's up to the job. When a birthday lands mid-month, can he keep the peace and the budget intact?
We humans are a subjective bunch and the animal kingdom is endless in its diversity, which makes the idea of pinpointing the world's cutest creature a major challenge! Can it be done?
Arthur embarks on a solitary quest to retrieve the Golden Trident from the Fisher King and prove himself worthy of the Camelot throne.

Louis prides himself on being a fun dad, but after he is forced stay home with the boys, he scrambles to find ways to entertain them. At Cattleman's Ranch, Jessica struggles to manage the staff and the new takeout service.
Sheldon fakes being sick to avoid a swim test at school. Meanwhile, Dr. Sturgis spies on Meemaw's new boyfriend.
Our heroes meet three sisters who grow berries with the help of a nearby group of Lotad!
The doctors reveal the incredible bit of body kit that keeps you balanced - your vestibular system, and find out what makes Team GB hockey star Shona McCallin superfast in today's 'Brilliant Bodies'.
Kiri, Lou and Sorry are playing tickle monster. They are very surprised when the grumpy Ichtheo wants to join in, and he's the best monster of all.
When a sardine swallows the key to a treasure chest, a humpback whale helps Kwazii track it down.
Now that Ginger knows his friends are the Peak City Heroes, he wants to know everything about them.

Gemma can't wait to explore on Snorkelling Day, but her snorkel gets in the way. Frizzy is being distracting while the cadets learn how to stay calm in the water, but in the end, it's Frizzy who teaches Gemma how to relax.
The PJs offer Armadylan a chance to try out for the hero team, but he's worried his clumsy strength will make it fail. So with Luna Girl's urging, he reluctantly reinvents himself as Moth Boy.
Miles's Father's Day fishing trip is interrupted by Doc Ock's plan to take over the harbor.
Bluey is excited to get her own room. But when bedtime comes, she misses Bingo more than she expected and must find a way to stay in touch with her sister.
Jonathan has lost his balloon. Paddington tries to get him a new one but accidentally ends up flying all over London. How will he get down? Pigeonton get help!
When a meteorite splashes into the sea Dad and Cosima cause problems by claiming it in the name of science, against the wishes of all the sea creatures.
The HexVets help an air collie and guinea pig discover the power of friendship.
Supertato shows the Grape Kids how to camp Supertato-style, but Evil Pea arrives and wows them with her ice camping. Before long, the Grape Kids need to be rescued by Supertato.

A tense night as Chris fights to save a policeman's poisoned pet, rescues a malnourished penguin that washed up onshore and operates on a young pup with a disintegrating leg.

Chris also introduces us to one of Bondi's most delightful dog-loving eccentrics, and a cutting-edge solution for a record-breaking goat.
Dr Chris desperately fights to save the life of an innocent hit and run victim. Lisa helps little Zoe battle a poisonous snake bite. And, a lorikeet learns to fly again.

A much-loved Labrador is in trouble after a head on collision with a car and Lisa is in a race against time to find the cause of a mystery illness that is threatening the life of a five-month-old kitten. As well, Chris heads to the bush and gets called out to help with a difficult birth.

It's an unforgettable story as Chris takes home a fragile baby kangaroo with the odds against him: will the joey make it without his mum? Plus, a helping hand for a puppy with a life-threatening problem. And Chris confronts his archenemy: a chihuahua with a mean streak.
Follow Chris behind bars and meet three beautiful pups who are changing prisoners' lives. Lisa struggles to save the life of a pregnant beagle. And, a bunny brings the Bondi vet to tears.

Chasing Dora is the story of three California surfers who decided to bring to life an epic challenge thrown down by one of surfing's greatest stylists, the renowned maverick, Miki Dora, who died in 2002 at age 67. Dora was one of the sport's iconic figures. He railed against the commercialization of surfing, yet endorsed one of the best-selling surfboard models of the mid-'60s surf boom; he decried competitive surfing, yet still chose to enter some, and floated schemes to promote others; he shunned publicity, yet managed to use the surf media to create an almost mythic persona for himself. Chasing Dora takes on one of his radical ideas--that the ultimate test of a truly great surfer would be in a contest for the longest wave ridden, on a self-made wooden board, with no equipment or accessories that stemmed from the industrial age--no plastics, no neoprene suits, no surf leashes.<br /><br />The challenge took the film's stars, Robert "Wingnut" Weaver, Marc Andreini, and Mickey Munoz, halfway around the world to Jeffreys Bay, South Africa, where they faced some of the largest swells of the year on their hand-made wood boards, wearing nothing but wool trunks and vests in frigid 50 degree water.<br /><br />But Chasing Dora is not just a film of retro whimsy. By a fortunate coincidence, the crew arrived at Jeffreys Bay just after a top-flight World Championship Tour event and many top pro surfers had stuck around to enjoy freesurfing in the fantastic conditions. Amazing contemporary action from World Champions Kelly Slater and Andy Irons stands in stark contrast to Dora's anachronistic challenge.<br /><br />One of the film's makers, Wes Brown, is grandson of Bruce Brown, whose mid-'60s movie The Endless Summer remains the most successful surf film of all time. Wes Brown's father, Dana, is also an accomplished documentary surf filmmaker, best known for his 2003 hit, Step Into Liquid.
In January 2020, Volcom released a psychedelic short film featuring the Brazilian surfer Yago Dora. A young athlete to follow closely as he makes his way among the best.

Grant, Jay and the rest of the TAPS team head to the Weston State Hospital, a now abandoned psychiatric facility in West Virginia, to investigate if the claims about the building are true; volunteers have reported seeing strange occurrences.

Jason, Grant and the TAPS team head to New England to answer a call from a terrified family plagued by mysterious apparitions. During their investigation, TAPS uncovers some shocking evidence of paranormal activity in the home. From there, they take on claims at the Palace Theater in Manchester, NH, a former vaudeville stop.

The Taps team heads to the coasts to tackle with two investigations. First they travel to Massachusetts to visit the Colonial Inn at Cape Cod. Then they head over to California to investigate the Moss Beach Distillery.

Grant, Jason and the TAPS team head to New Jersey for their next investigation into the paranormal as they spend the night in the home of the last royal governor and look for evidence of hauntings before they examine the Red Mill Museum.

TAPS embarks on an investigation at Fort Delaware, built in the mid-1800?s and primarily used as an artillery defense for the Union during the Civil War. It eventually became a Civil War POW camp, housing over 33,000 Confederate soldiers. The conditions at Fort Delaware were grim, and it soon gained a reputation in the Confederacy as a ?black hole.?

A local preservation society took over this property in 2000, and discovered over 30 boxes of unclaimed human remains tucked away in the basement bathroom. Renovations unearthed remnants of the Episcopal church as well as light fixtures and stained glass that'd been hidden behind the walls and ceilings as if the original funeral director created a building within a building.

TAPS goes to Connecticut to unravel the mysteries at the historic Pettibone Tavern. Built in 1780, the tavern originally served as a carriage stop between Albany and Boston during the late 18th century. During this time, it was also supposedly the site of a brutal axe murder, and through the years, employees have consistently reported activity that they cannot explain.
TAPS visits a 16th century North Kingstown, R.I., landmark to solve an awful mystery. Then, TAPS comes to help a military family living in Groton, Conn.

TAPS visits the abandoned (and skeevy) remains of an art-deco masterpiece, Buffalo Central Terminal. The terminal, a 14-story combination office tower/train station, opened in 1929 and closed 50 years later. After falling through the hands of various owners, the Central Terminal Restoration Corp. acquired it in 1997. In the years since the Terminal's abandonment, it has become a potent source of paranormal stories.

TAPS is in Florida to investigate an inn that is a hotbed of paranormal activity. This unique St. Petersburg property consists of two multi-story Victorian manors: the Pink House and the Purple House. They were both built in the late 1800s, and are believed to house more than just customers.

Paranormal investigators Grant Wilson and Jason Hawes attempt to find evidence of supernatural activity at a plantation home where a tour group consisting of 35 visitors claim to have witnessed a candlestick flying across the room.

Heather Tracy and her family moved into her ancestor's property two years ago. There were always reports of odd activity and it soon became apparent to her that there was something more to the stories.

TAPS investigates a landmark pool hall in team member Steve Gonsalves' hometown. Over the years, the first floor fronted several retail clients, but is now a tavern called Theodore's. Though two separate establishments, Theodore's and Smith's have a common problem; they both experience intense paranormal activity. Now, their owners are working together and asking TAPS to diagnose their decades-old problem.

TAPS returns to investigate another legendary haunted naval landmark--the aircraft carrier USS Hornet in Alameda, CA. The Hornet, the eighth vessel to carry her name, was commissioned at the height of World War II in 1943. She quickly became one of the most highly decorated ships in the Navy and the USS Hornet is considered the most haunted ship in the Navy, past or present.
TAPS heads to Topsfield, Massachusetts to investigate an old haunted farmhouse.

When natural disasters leave communities reeling, pilot Gareth Fletcher and the Convoy of Hope swing into action. This episode takes you to the heart of crisis-stricken areas, where Gareth's willingness to get involved sees him join together with others to help rebuild not just homes, but hope. Witness the incredible power of community spirit in the face of adversity.

Peter talks with Aron Mercer from Xceptional to learn how their experience with finding roles for neurodiverse job seekers has transformed their mindset to building teams. Peter and the team explore how a strengths based team can be the catalyst for accelerated business success.

Dominating the landscape for centuries, ancient cathedrals and abbeys reflect Britain's turbulent history through their architectural grandeur. A Pilgrimage through Britain's Great Cathedrals explores cathedrals and abbeys found throughout England and Wales, featuring interviews with historians and experts and breathtaking footage of the cathedrals' legendary facades and soaring interior spaces.

p.t: Walking in the Footsteps of Faith
p.d: It all started with the blending of three passions: a passion for History, a passion for Adventure and a passion for Faith Works and teaching! Steve Faucette always dreamed of hosting a show and sharing it with the world. Discover how giants of the faith like Mother Theresa, Martin Luther, and David Livingston lived following Steve, walking in their footsteps!

A panel of women get together to share their lives, struggles, families, And the joy that occurs throughout their daily lives, And they also want to dig deeper to build a sense of community where they can work on relationships And their faith.

Pastor Joseph Prince preaches dynamic messages centred on the pure gospel of the grace of God. His desire is to help believers understand grace and how greatly blessed, highly favoured and deeply loved they are by their heavenly Father.

Documents the fortress plateau of Masada, where Jewish Zealots faced their Roman nemeses. These ruins provide archaeological evidence for the histories of Josephus, offering profound lessons on courage and where to place one's faith.

Katherine Ruonala shares a practical message of love and hope to the nations. Reaching across denominational walls, her ministry is used to spread the fires of revival and ignite a fresh passion in the hearts of believers to go deeper in their relationship with God. Katherine carries a strong prophetic and miracle anointing with many experiencing instant healing in her meetings.
Are you properly dressed to do spiritual battle? Today, Joyce teaches on the importance of our words and how to fight the enemy and win by speaking the Word of God.

Inspired by an extraordinary true story, Sound of Hope: The Story of Possum Trot reveals what can happen when one family’s act of faith inspires an entire community. In the small East Texas community of Possum Trot, Donna and Reverend W.C. Martin open their hearts and home to children in the foster care system. Their decision soon sparks something remarkable within their church, as family after family steps forward to welcome children desperately needing a place to belong. Together, 22 families adopt 77 children, many considered among the most difficult to place, creating a powerful movement of compassion that reaches far beyond their tiny community. Sound of Hope is a deeply moving celebration of faith, family, perseverance and the extraordinary difference ordinary people can make when they choose to act.

The season's first challenge finds the contestants slicing halibut into thin six-ounce fillets. One member of each team must serve as maître d' during the dining service.

Starting with live chickens in their sleeping quarters, the teams must pluck and clean the birds perfectly before serving them family style at dinner; the winning team takes some time off while the losers take to the fields to pick peppers.

The red and blue teams prepare pasta for the evening dinner service, and the team with the highest output earns a day at the Santa Monica Pier; one team's chances are jeopardized when an accident in the kitchen sends a contestant to the hospital.
The first challenge for the remaining eleven chefs: make a gourmet pizza. The winners enjoy gourmet burgers in Santa Barbara while the losers prepare for the night's dinner service.

When a picky 16-year-old comes to Hell’s Kitchen for her fantasy birthday bash, the chefs find themselves catering to one of their toughest critics yet...teenagers. The two teams must call on their inner-adolescent to design a teen-pleasing menu for the girl’s special day.
Chef Ramsay makes the nine remaining chefs take a blindfolded taste test. The winners get to go to a spa; the losers must clean the dorm.

The group dynamics are drastically changed when Chef Ramsey asks for a volunteer to switch sides. This week's challenge consists of creating 4 new dishes from 20 ingredients. One chef requires a medic after injuring himself during the challenge.

It's all about speed and accuracy as the teams are challenged to prepare dishes in a relay race. The winners are treated to a day of fun in the sun as they head to the beach for private surfing lessons. The losing team is forced to get down and dirty and clean the entire restaurant.

To give the remaining chefs a little added inspiration, Chef Ramsay takes them to the future location of The London West Hollywood; while in the kitchen, a chef burns his hand and the others struggle to deliver food to the diners in a timely manner.

Brace for fallout as Tammy blows a gasket after Courtney is rude to Jamie and Alex. In Alberta, Megan isn't as lucky finding new employment as she'd hoped, and feels the stress as she finally decides to head home.
Megan swallows her pride and asks for her job back at Wendigo Farms. Tammy's hot young date shows up at the barn uninvited. Allie briefs Mike on a drastic strategy for winning Tammy back.
Two members of Hope's team travel to England, discovering new techniques and making allies on the front lines.

A tiny kitten has been found abandoned in a cardboard box, and Chris is shocked at the extent of her injuries. She desperately needs surgery to try to repair her shattered leg. Then it's a heartwarming search to find her a new home.

Julien And Nicolette have three daughters, and Keira, 4, has an irrational fear of dogs. Dr. Lisa advises that the best thing to do might be to get a dog. Will the cure work and what special issues do three young girls put in her way?

Fulfil a dream as Dr Chris travels to the UK to work at a vet clinic in Cornwall, tending to dairy calves, a prize-winning duck, a Siberian eagle owl and Atlantic grey seals. Then head to Yorkshire to see horses race over the moors.

Meet Bruce a cat who took a leap from a third-floor window, and see how Dr. Scott helps him get back in shape. Then sit in on an emergency caesarean section for first-time dog mama Bonnie, who needs help delivering six puppies.

Tuxedos at the ready as Mythbusters take on 007 in this Bond special. Our stealthy agents are on a mission to explode the myths about Bond's gadgets, getaways and guns. Licensed to thrill— you'll be shaken AND stirred.
In this episode of Mythbusters, surfs up dude! Kari, Tori and Grant take on a gnarly Internet myth, they’re testing if a couple of sticks of dynamite can create ideal surfing conditions.
It’s a three-myth blockbuster episode! Adam and Jamie wrestle at the controls of a controversial myth and then the guys tackle the monster myth, Airplane on a Conveyor Belt!
On the first Viewer’s Special, Episode #85, we tested a bunch of myths from the fan site, and it was a blast, literally. But fortunately, for every myth we test, our fans have a bunch more.
On this reverential episode of MythBusters, we pay tribute to the man who could make something really useful from almost anything: MacGyver!

The MythBusters ‘Upfront Special’ is a giant two hour feast where the team orders everything SUPERSIZED. Jamie and Adam go all the way to Cape Town, home of some of biggest sharks in the world, to test ‘Great White’ myths.

Alaska is the very definition of intense. With more volcanoes than any other State, a gaggle of gynormous glaciers and enough wildlife to make David Attenborough salivate, it’s without doubt, one of the most intense places on earth.

On this episode, the Moon Landing Hoax Hour the team tackle the tallest tale of all! On July the 16th 1969 the world watched as three brave astronauts headed for the moon Neil Armstrong took his first tentative extra terrestrial steps.
The Mythbusters invite a real-life ninja to help them test even more shadow warrior myths. Can a ninja really catch an arrow, and could a ninja assassinate someone from underwater?
Adam and Jamie re-enact a famous scene from Scent Of A Woman to find out if you can drive while blind.

On this episode of Mythbusters, we give internet viral videos a timely check-up. They’re exciting, funny, and sometimes barely credible. We can’t wait to pass them on to our ten best friends, but can we truly believe everything we see?

On this episode of Mythbusters Adam and Jamie take a fan mail film and use it to dial in on a phone book fable. And then Kari, Grant and Tory test a fishy tale of Hollywood pyrotechnics with their own big bang theories.
Adam and Jamie test whether a stun gun can be water-powered, while Kari, Grant, and Tory examine if fire extinguishers explode when dropped in flames and whether fire walking is mind over matter.
Does drinking alcohol make people look more attractive? Do alleged ways of sobering up really work? Could ancient Korean hwacha actually do what is claimed of it?

Adam and Jamie take on Indiana Jones to find out if you can flip a motorcycle by jamming a flagpole into its spinning wheel. While Kari, Tory and Grant try to break out of prison using only bed sheets, toilet paper and hair!
The source of the Mekong River is high up in the Tibetan plateau, from there it flows into Yunnan Province, China, where our journey begins.
This is a country of outstanding natural beauty and the Mekong carves out pockets of ancient forest that provide refuge for some of the most beautiful and elusive creatures on Earth.
For people who live on active volcanoes, life has an element of impermanence to it. There is always the fear that one day their turn will come, and their home will be in the path of the volcano.
Watch a desert landscape transform into a lush frenzy of feeding and breeding.
It sometimes feels like mammals rule the world; there are well over 5,000 species, colonising every corner of the globe. But in Arabia there’s a different story – this is a land where reptiles rule.

The Arabian Desert is one of the most challenging places on earth, but the animals here are resilient and specialized. Even for the hardiest inhabitants, death’s never far away. Creatures must seize every opportunity to find food, shelter and water. Adaptability is the key to dune survival.
Spoonbill Soft Shoe Shuffle: The team help a trio of troubled baby wallabies and a koala having seizures. Plus, a kookaburra has surgery and a spoonbill gets corrective shoes.
The clinic deals with the aftermath of a Brisbane flood, while a baby kangaroo is in need of round-the-clock care. Vet Karina tackles the turtle waiting list.
Vet Karina fights to save a koala mauled by dogs. Plus, rescue Chantel tries to pick up a peeved possum, while vet Meaghan bonds with a gaggle of goslings.

This is the story of the “Golden Forest”, the vast expanses of kelp that lines Africa’s southwestern shore. Fed by an upwelling of nutrients from deep in the Atlantic, the kelp forest nurtures four distinct worlds.
Epic natural wonders are uncovered in the remote American southwest desert. From vast canyons bound by towering cliffs to red striped fossilized dunes, the Paria Plateau is a geologic marvel.
Nova Scotia's wetlands, home to the Blanding's turtle, are at risk. But if the turtles can make it through their tough first years, they'll live for almost a century.
A look at the complex relationships between lobsters, scallops and crabs and how changing temperatures are bringing invasive species to the ocean.
At the southern edge of the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland on Earth, there's a place like no other, and a wildlife so diverse scientists scramble to understand it.
The Pantanal is the largest tropical wetland on Earth, yet it's also one of the most unforgiving habitats to call home.

In this episode of Spiky Gold Hunters, the crew of the San Nicholas are heading to the southern most part of Stewart Island, the last stop before Antarctica. Despite the icy waters and cold conditions, the competition between the divers is fierce although for one member of the team it will be their last trip.

In the first part of the episode, Andy explores sustainable kingfish farming in Spencer Gulf, South Australia, visiting Clean Seas sea farm and preparing fresh kingfish sashimi with the team. Moving to Kangaroo Island, he learns pickling techniques with Kate from Kangaroo Island Source, showcasing her products in a Carne Asada Taco. The episode continues with Andy exploring d'Arenberg's multi-function building and 'The Cube,' experiencing a Chef's Table, and concludes at Wirra Wirra winery, where he cooks Yogurt Flatbread with Olive Oil and Dukka, enjoying it with the staff and their wines.

In Kakadu National Park, Andy joins Dewayne Webb foraging pandanus and cooking Seared Buffalo with Pandanus & Charred Herb Salsa over an open fire. He then heads to Darwin, assisting Zach Green at Elijah's Kitchen, a food truck offering indigenous-inspired meals like Magpie Goose and Crocodile Laksa. Returning to Kakadu, Andy goes fishing with local Barramundi expert Rob Johnson and prepares Paperbark Leaf BBQ Barramundi with Sour Tamarind Sauce at Anbangbang Billabong, showcasing the region's environment and produce.
